title: Nile landforms and travel

sources.title: Assigned OER Ancient Egypt
sources.status: Named pages content-read; full course audit incomplete

teach: A delta is land deposited by a river near its mouth. The Nile Delta lies in northern Egypt, where the river reaches the Mediterranean Sea.
As the river slows, it can leave sediment and split into channels. The delta’s fertile land supported farming. A delta is not the same as rocky rapids upstream.
Cataracts are rocky rapids or rough stretches of a river. They can make travel by boat difficult. In this unit they are a geography term, not a medical term.
A route affected by cataracts may require travelers to change how they move goods. The Nile connected regions, but not every stretch was equally easy to navigate.
